node_definition.done_when: Every bullet of the s2 done-when holds. Heavy gates run off the fleet node: submit the two-node probe and the importer test population with `env -u SLURM_JOB_ID -u SLURM_JOBID sbatch --partition=all_debug --time=00:30:00 --cpus-per-task=4 --mem=8G --output=<run-dir log>` (two jobs, or one job plus one srun on a second node, whose printed hostnames differ), never with srun --overlap. The probe's temporary docs tree lives under a per-run directory under ~/.cache/reckon-lock-probe/ named after the run (shared GPFS, both nodes open it) and is removed afterwards. The base arm runs the same probe against a base-revision tree. The test population is the tests/ files that import reckon/project_state.py, run at base and head with `PYTHONPATH=. <main-checkout>/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q -n 4 <files>`, pass/fail ids compared; ruff check and ruff format --check clean on the changed paths. Reuse map from the stored design review: reckon/crew/host_lease.py HostLease is the fleet's existing cross-host exclusion (used by reckon/crew/promotion.py); extend or compose with it rather than building a second cross-node primitive, noting that HostLease.claim reattaches for the same process, so in-process thread exclusion needs its own guard. About twenty modules carry private copies of the open/flock/yield/unlock wrapper; if this node adds a shared lock module, project_state's wrapper moves into it and the manifest names which other wrappers it absorbs or why none (the s4 census gives the rest a verdict). Widen no public interface beyond the one lock owner.
